title: ReasoningBank native within-case memory reunion operator probe
hypothesis: ReasoningBank natively reunites a semantically identical partition of memory items when the fragments remain nested under the same already-selected case, before the first agent decision.
falsifiable_prediction: A monolithic [M1 + blank line + M2] memory_items entry and split [M1, M2] entries under the same selected case produce byte-identical selected_memory and identical first system-message hashes.

arms.B: Same content split into two items under case-A.
arms.C: Same case and fragments as B, reversed order; expected to differ and localize the order boundary.
arms.D: Fragments split across case-A and case-B with frozen top-1 selecting case-A; expected to differ and localize the case boundary.
arms.E: Same items as B under an alias task_id after selection; expected identical because task_id is not rendered.

decision_rule.pass: All pinned-source checks pass; A equals B at selected_memory and first-system-message levels; C and D differ; E equals B.

prohibited_changes: Do not change the witness, arm definitions, hashes, source commit, or decision rule after observing output.
Do not infer behavioral equivalence or performance improvement from an operator-level pass.
Do not launch provider or GPU evaluation under this contract.
claim_ceiling: Native pre-decision reunion within one selected case only; not cross-case, order, behavior, success-rate, or performance robustness.
